_comment: FICTIONAL demo context. Service names, owners and dependency policy are invented and are not a claim about vLLM's real architecture or ownership. Paths mirror vLLM's public layout so the pack also works against a real clone.

contextPack.name: Inference serving platform (synthetic demo pack)
contextPack.disclaimer: Architecture, decisions, ownership and policy in this pack are fictional and invented for a demo. They are not vLLM's real architecture or ownership, and no real person or team is named.

services.name: api-gateway
services.description: Public HTTP surface. Owns the request/response contracts clients depend on.

services.name: serving-common
services.description: Shared HTTP plumbing: dependencies, cancellation, load-aware dispatch.

services.name: request-validation
services.description: The validation gate. Every inference request is accepted or rejected here before it reaches the engine.

services.name: request-render
services.description: Turns caller-supplied messages and prompts into engine inputs.

services.name: engine-core
services.description: Request lifecycle, admission control and the step loop. Fronted by the AsyncLLM facade.

services.name: scheduler
services.description: Continuous batching, the request queue and KV cache accounting.

services.name: executor
services.description: Forward-pass execution across one or many processes.

services.name: observability
services.description: Metrics, tracing and structured logging. Depended on by everything; depends on nothing.

compat.policy: Request and response models under vllm/entrypoints are the published HTTP contract. Removing or renaming a field, removing a route, or adding a required request field are all breaking changes for existing clients.
AsyncLLM is the only engine entry point the serving layer may use, so its public signature is a contract across a service boundary.
SchedulerInterface and SchedulerOutput are what the engine is allowed to assume about any scheduler. Changing them changes every scheduler implementation.
